Taki-o-Autahi.t: Drawn on the Southern Cross. Māori know the Cross as Māhutonga, and as the anchor, Te Punga, of Tama-rereti's canoe, the Milky Way; Autahi, in Stellarium's list of Māori names, is Canopus.
Taki-o-Autahi.c: Wikipedia, “Crux” (Māori section), after Elsdon Best, The Astronomical Knowledge of the Maori (Dominion Museum Monograph 3, 1922); Stellarium's Māori sky culture

Te Taura-o-te-waka-o-tamarereti.t: The rope of Tama-rereti's canoe: the two Pointers, Alpha and Beta Centauri, that tie the anchor, the Southern Cross, to the canoe of the Milky Way.
Te Taura-o-te-waka-o-tamarereti.c: Wikipedia, “Crux” and “Milky Way in mythology”, after Elsdon Best (1922)

Tau-toro.t: Orion's belt. Stellarium's list of Māori names gives Tau toro for the belt, among other names for parts of Orion (Hao-o-rua, Te Kakau).
Tau-toro.c: Stellarium's Māori sky culture (its table of names)

The Great Boat of Tama Rereti.t: The tail of Scorpius: the canoe whose length is the Milky Way. Caught far from home as night fell, before there were any stars, Tama-rereti steered up the river that runs into the heavens and flung bright stones from the lake's edge over the darkness. Ranginui, the sky, was pleased, and placed the canoe up there as well, as a reminder of how the stars began.
The Great Boat of Tama Rereti.c: Wikipedia, “Milky Way in mythology” (Māori), after Elsdon Best (1922)

The Sail of Tainui.t: A maori constellation without a European counterpart. It is a sea voyaging catamaran. The belt of orion is the keel, the hyades is a claw sail and the Pleiades is the bow.
